prediction.likelyOutcome: EQY should win on liability against both Williamson and Gore and recover the large majority of the pleaded $170,484.37, because the Lease expressly charges the defaulting tenant with 'free rent or concessions' and Williamson has no evidence of the value of Hallmark's build-out or that the space could have been relet sooner — and under Austin Hill Country Realty the burden on both points is the tenant's. Expect a judgment in the $165,000-$255,000 range inclusive of a contractual fee award, with the realistic downside being a judge-driven partial haircut on the July-December 2024 overlap months rather than the full $62,096.52 offset. The dominant practical risk is not the merits but collectibility against Gore.

issues.label: Breach of Lease and Guaranty — Uncontested Rent Portion
Lockout Exposure (Not Currently Pleaded as a Counterclaim)
Collectibility Against Gore and the Tenant Entity

outcome.description: After a bench trial the court awarded the landlord $170,484.37 in past-due rent, the full amount it sought, with no credit for the $62,096.52 free-rent overlap offset or the $20,000 personal property. It also awarded $86,725.00 in attorney's fees. On appeal the rent damages were affirmed and the fee award reversed.
